strings.name: Carol Tomé
strings.role: UPS chief executive officer and former Home Depot chief financial officer
strings.summary: Carol Tomé is an American executive who long led finance at Home Depot and became UPS CEO in 2020. Her work concerns parcel networks, customer mix and labor negotiations. UPS's operational changes have also involved workforce reductions and transformation costs, so scale or profit alone cannot describe their impact.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026; recent evidence is the October 27 earnings release and its quotations from her. Board membership and CEO duties, and reported and adjusted profit, are distinguished. Donation commitments and future financial guidance are not recorded as realized outcomes.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads UPS logistics operations, contributing to global parcel transport, e-commerce delivery and corporate management.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Graduated in communications from the University of Wyoming in 1979; earned a University of Denver MBA in 1981, focusing on finance.
strings.facts.f2.label: Other governance roles
strings.facts.f2.value: Current independent Verizon director and Finance Committee member; Cisco and Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta directorships are former roles, not CEO positions at those institutions.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Network changes and employee impact
strings.highlights.h1.text: In 2026 UPS said it had completed its Amazon volume reduction and network reconfiguration. Second-quarter transformation charges mainly concerned separation costs from workforce reductions; operational improvements must be presented alongside employee effects.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Joint labor bargaining
strings.highlights.h2.text: The 2023 contract addressed pay and safety protections through company-union negotiations and member voting; its achievements cannot all be attributed to the CEO personally.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Third-quarter results released
strings.timeline.t1.text: UPS reported $22.9 billion revenue and approximately $1.7 billion operating profit; adjusted operating profit was about $2.1 billion. The raised full-year outlook remained a forecast.
strings.timeline.t2.title: University reports joint gift commitment
strings.timeline.t2.text: The University of Wyoming reported her and Ramon's joint $20 million commitment to its scholars program, announced in spring; the first business-school cohort was planned for 2027.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Labor contract fully ratified
strings.timeline.t3.text: Members approved the national master agreement on August 22 and the final supplement on August 25; these were separate steps.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Became UPS CEO
strings.timeline.t4.text: The appointment announced March 12 took effect, succeeding David Abney; Abney remained executive chairman during the transition.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Retired from Home Depot
strings.timeline.t5.text: Ended her long finance leadership tenure, succeeded by Richard McPhail; became UPS CEO the following year.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined the UPS board
strings.timeline.t6.text: Participated in governance as a director before later taking the top day-to-day executive role.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Promoted to Home Depot CFO
strings.timeline.t7.text: Advanced from finance management to chief financial officer; her 1995 joining date is not the start of her CFO tenure.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joined Home Depot
strings.timeline.t8.text: Became vice president and treasurer, later expanding her financial-management responsibilities.
